newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin sees new NBP, banks law before polls.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin sees new NBP, banks law before polls.

text.p: Poland's parliament is likely to pass an amended banking law and a new bill on the National Bank of Poland before parliamentary polls due in this year's final quarter, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday.

The current laws created at the start of Poland's transformation into a market economy from communist central planning are in many aspects outdated and bankers say they hamper the development of the banking system.

"The banking law is at the final stage of preparation and I expect it will be cleared by the government economic committee on Monday, then by the whole cabinet and it will go to parliament," Belka told a group of foreign journalists.
"The law on the NBP is now half-way through parliamentary committees, which wait for the banking law draft to continue work on both of them because they are complementary," he said.
"I hope both will be voted into law before parliamentary elections," Belka added.
